# Metric inventory: iam-audit-log

<!-- Generated by `make metrics-inventory` (.github/scripts/metrics-inventory.py) from the
     Platform Observability Registry in platform-gincommon v2.0.0 and a real /metrics
     scrape of this service. Do not edit; CI fails when this file is out of date. -->

Every series carries the centrally injected const labels `domain` (`iam`), `service` (`iam-audit-log`) and `environment`. The tables list each metric's own labels only. Status is the registry's: `approved`, or `proposed` (awaiting observability-governance ratification). Tier 3 metrics are this service's own and need no registry entry. See [README.md](README.md) for how the tiers are built and enforced.

## Tier 1: platform-shared metrics (emitted by the platform libraries)

The libraries record these on the shared registry (`gincommon.MetricsRegisterer()`). Metrics marked *service-built* are constructed by this service from the registry (`gincommon.NewShared*Vec`, `registry.go` `PlatformRegistry`) before platform-events registers, so the library adopts the same collector and both record into one series set. platform-events registers its publisher and outbox collectors in every process; here they stay at zero, because this service publishes nothing (AL-INV-10).

| Metric | Emitted by | Type | Status | Labels | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `platform_build_info` | platform-gincommon | gauge | proposed | `version` | Always 1; the version label carries the build of the emitting service. |
| `platform_http_requests_total` | platform-gincommon | counter | proposed | `method`, `route`, `status_class`, `error_class` | HTTP requests completed by the server, including recovered panics (counted as 5xx). |
| `platform_http_request_duration_seconds` | platform-gincommon | histogram (request_duration) | proposed | `method`, `route`, `status_class`, `error_class` | HTTP server request latency in seconds, measured by MetricsMiddleware. |
| `platform_http_request_size_bytes` | platform-gincommon | histogram (payload_size) | proposed | `method`, `route`, `status_class`, `error_class` | HTTP request body size in bytes from Content-Length (not observed when the length is unknown, e.g. chunked uploads). |
| `platform_http_response_size_bytes` | platform-gincommon | histogram (payload_size) | proposed | `method`, `route`, `status_class`, `error_class` | HTTP response body size in bytes. |
| `platform_http_active_requests` | platform-gincommon | gauge | proposed | `route` | HTTP requests currently being handled. |
| `platform_http_panics_total` | platform-gincommon | counter | proposed | `method`, `route` | HTTP handler panics recovered by the middleware stack. |
| `platform_http_rate_limited_requests_total` | platform-gincommon | counter | proposed | `method`, `route` | HTTP requests answered with 429 Too Many Requests. |
| `platform_http_request_timeouts_total` | platform-gincommon | counter | proposed | `method`, `route` | HTTP requests whose TimeoutMiddleware deadline expired before the handler responded. |
| `platform_unclassified_errors_total` | platform-gincommon | counter | approved | `transport` | Errors that reached the top-level error handler unclassified and were answered as a generic internal error (HTTP 500 internal-error, gRPC Internal): a programming defect. |
| `platform_messages_received_total` | platform-events | counter | approved | `queue` | A message delivered to a consumer by its queue (one per SQS delivery, redeliveries included), counted on receipt before it is parsed. |
| `platform_messages_processed_total` | platform-events | counter | approved | `queue`, `event_type` | A received message whose handler completed successfully, after which the message was acknowledged (deleted). Messages dead-lettered instead are counted in platform_dlq_messages_total, not here. |
| `platform_messages_failed_total` | platform-events | counter | approved | `queue`, `event_type`, `reason` | A received message that could not be processed on this delivery, by reason: malformed (not a valid envelope), decode_error (schema-registry codec failure), handler_error, handler_panic, or dead_letter_error (dead-letter handling or DLQ forwarding failed). A failed message is retried or dead-lettered; see platform_retry_total and platform_dlq_messages_total. |
| `platform_retry_total` | platform-events | counter | approved | `operation`, `event_type` | An attempt that failed and was left for automatic retry: a consumed message whose processing failed and stays on its queue for redelivery (operation=consume), or an outbox publish that failed with attempts remaining (operation=outbox_publish). |
| `platform_dlq_messages_total` | platform-events, *service-built* | counter | approved | `operation`, `event_type`, `reason` | A message moved to dead-letter storage: forwarded to its SQS queue's RedrivePolicy DLQ (operation=consume), or moved to outbox_dead_letters after exhausting its publish attempts (operation=outbox_publish), by reason. |
| `platform_duplicate_messages_total` | platform-events, *service-built* | counter | proposed | `queue`, `event_type` | A redelivered message acknowledged without running its handler because the consumer's dedup ledger (inbox processed_events) had already recorded its event ID. |
| `platform_dependency_request_seconds` | platform-events, *service-built* | histogram (dependency_request) | proposed | `dependency`, `operation`, `outcome` | Client-observed wall time of one call to an external dependency — SNS (publish, publish_batch), SQS (receive_message, delete_message, change_message_visibility, send_message, get_queue_attributes, get_queue_url) or the configured schema-registry codec (encode, decode) — by outcome. The _count series counts calls. receive_message is a long poll: its duration includes up to WaitTimeSeconds (default 20 s) of waiting on an empty queue, so exclude it from latency views (it stays meaningful for error rates). |
| `platform_event_propagation_seconds` | platform-events | histogram (event_propagation) | proposed | `queue`, `event_type` | Time from an event's creation (envelope `time`, set by the producer) to its FIRST receipt by a consumer (ApproximateReceiveCount ≤ 1) — end-to-end propagation delay through the outbox, SNS and SQS. Redeliveries are not observed, so retry delay does not inflate it. Negative clock skew is clamped to 0. |
| `platform_queue_depth` | platform-events, *service-built* | gauge | proposed | `queue` | Messages waiting on a consumer's queue to be received (SQS ApproximateNumberOfMessages — visible, not in flight or delayed), sampled by the consumer every WithQueueDepthMetrics interval. Approximate by SQS design. |
| `platform_dlq_depth` | platform-events, *service-built* | gauge | proposed | `queue` | Messages sitting in the dead-letter queue attached to a consumer's queue by its RedrivePolicy (SQS ApproximateNumberOfMessages of the DLQ), sampled with platform_queue_depth. queue is the SOURCE queue's name, so the gauge joins with the consumer's other queue metrics. |
| `platform_messages_in_flight` | platform-events | gauge | proposed | `queue` | Messages a consumer has received and is currently processing (decode, dead-letter routing or handler), per replica. At the consumer's concurrency limit for long periods means the replica is saturated; a value that never drops points at a hung handler (see WithHandlerTimeout). |
| `platform_messages_published_total` | platform-events | counter | proposed | `topic`, `event_type`, `outcome`<br>`outcome` ∈ `success`, `error` | One event a producer attempted to publish to a topic, by outcome (error includes validation, encoding and broker failures; a batch counts each message). |
| `platform_message_processing_duration_seconds` | platform-events | histogram (message_processing) | proposed | `queue`, `event_type` | Wall time a consumer's handler (or dead-letter handler) spent on one delivery, whatever the outcome. |
| `platform_outbox_pending_events` | platform-events | gauge | proposed | - | Events in a service's transactional outbox that are due to be published (unpublished, not leased and not waiting out a retry backoff), sampled every outbox GaugeInterval (default 15s) and capped at 100000 (a reading of 100000 means at least that many). Left at its last value when the count query fails (see platform_outbox_errors_total{operation="pending_count"}). |
| `platform_outbox_leased_events` | platform-events | gauge | proposed | - | Unpublished outbox events not yet due: claimed by a runner and being published, or waiting out a retry backoff. Sampled every GaugeInterval, capped at 100000. |
| `platform_outbox_oldest_pending_age` | platform-events | gauge | proposed | - | Age of the oldest unpublished outbox event (now − created_at), 0 when nothing is unpublished, sampled every GaugeInterval. Transient publish failures never dead-letter, so this is the signal that delivery has stopped even when the backlog is small (e.g. a credential outage on a low-volume service). |
| `platform_outbox_ordering_blocked_events` | platform-events | gauge | proposed | - | Ordered outbox events (outbox.EnqueueOrdered) waiting behind an earlier unpublished record with the same ordering key. Sampled every GaugeInterval, capped at 100000. A value that keeps growing means a key's head record keeps failing and holds the rest of its key. |
| `platform_message_timeouts_total` | platform-events | counter | proposed | `queue`, `event_type`, `operation`<br>`operation` ∈ `decode`, `dead_letter_handler`, `handler` | A received message whose WithHandlerTimeout deadline expired, by the stage it expired in: decode (codec decode), dead_letter_handler, or handler. Each is also counted in platform_messages_failed_total under its usual reason (decode_error, dead_letter_error, handler_error) — this counter separates timeouts from other failures without changing that Canonical metric's vocabulary. |
| `platform_outbox_publish_attempts_total` | platform-events | counter | proposed | `event_type`, `outcome`<br>`outcome` ∈ `success`, `error` | One attempt by the outbox runner to publish a claimed outbox event, by outcome. |
| `platform_outbox_errors_total` | platform-events | counter | proposed | `operation`<br>`operation` ∈ `poll`, `unmarshal`, `mark_published`, `pending_count`, `leased_count`, `oldest_pending`, `blocked_count` | An outbox runner step that failed outside a publish attempt: poll (claiming a batch), unmarshal (a stored envelope that no longer parses), mark_published (an event published but not marked — it will be delivered again), pending_count / leased_count / oldest_pending / blocked_count (a gauge query). |
| `platform_outbox_dead_letter_operations_total` | platform-events | counter | proposed | `operation`<br>`operation` ∈ `reprocess`, `discard` | Outbox dead-letter records acted on by an operator call: reprocess (moved back to outbox_events for retry) or discard (permanently deleted). Counts records, not calls. |
| `platform_telemetry_label_overflow_total` | platform-events | counter | proposed | `label`<br>`label` ∈ `event_type` | A label value the library replaced because it exceeded its cardinality bound: event_type over 128 bytes → `__oversized__`, or a new distinct event_type beyond the per-process limit (default 200) → `__other__`. Counts replacements. Non-zero means a misconfigured or adversarial producer, or a limit set below the service's real number of event types. |
| `platform_library_info` | platform-events | gauge | proposed | `library`, `library_version` | Always 1. Identifies a platform library and the version a service was built with, for fleet-wide upgrade tracking. |
| `platform_db_queries_total` | platform-pgcommon | counter | proposed | `pool`, `operation`, `outcome`<br>`operation` ∈ `ALTER`, `ANALYZE`, `BEGIN`, `CALL`, `COMMENT`, `COMMIT`, `COPY`, `CREATE`, `DELETE`, `DISCARD`, `DO`, `DROP`, `END`, `EXPLAIN`, `GRANT`, `INSERT`, `LISTEN`, `LOCK`, `MERGE`, `NOTIFY`, `PREPARE`, `REFRESH`, `RELEASE`, `RESET`, `REVOKE`, `ROLLBACK`, `SAVEPOINT`, `SELECT`, `SET`, `SHOW`, `START`, `TABLE`, `TRUNCATE`, `UNLISTEN`, `UPDATE`, `VACUUM`, `VALUES`, `WITH`, `BATCH`, `other`<br>`outcome` ∈ `success`, `error` | One statement a service executed against PostgreSQL through a pgcommon pool — a query, a SendBatch (operation=BATCH) or a CopyFrom (operation=COPY) — counted when it completes, by outcome. Statements pgcommon issues itself (RLS GUC set_config on acquire, BEGIN / COMMIT / ROLLBACK, transaction timeouts, savepoints, the PgBouncer wrapping transaction) are excluded unless they fail: a failed COMMIT or GUC injection is a failure of the caller's work. |
| `platform_db_query_duration_seconds` | platform-pgcommon | histogram (db_query) | proposed | `pool`, `operation`<br>`operation` ∈ `ALTER`, `ANALYZE`, `BEGIN`, `CALL`, `COMMENT`, `COMMIT`, `COPY`, `CREATE`, `DELETE`, `DISCARD`, `DO`, `DROP`, `END`, `EXPLAIN`, `GRANT`, `INSERT`, `LISTEN`, `LOCK`, `MERGE`, `NOTIFY`, `PREPARE`, `REFRESH`, `RELEASE`, `RESET`, `REVOKE`, `ROLLBACK`, `SAVEPOINT`, `SELECT`, `SET`, `SHOW`, `START`, `TABLE`, `TRUNCATE`, `UNLISTEN`, `UPDATE`, `VACUUM`, `VALUES`, `WITH`, `BATCH`, `other` | Client-observed wall time of one statement (query, SendBatch or CopyFrom) against PostgreSQL through a pgcommon pool, from send to result. Library-internal statements (RLS GUC set_config, BEGIN / COMMIT / ROLLBACK, transaction timeouts, savepoints) are excluded unless they fail: a failed COMMIT or GUC injection is a failure of the caller's work. |
| `platform_db_pool_acquires_total` | platform-pgcommon | counter | proposed | `pool`, `outcome`<br>`outcome` ∈ `success`, `error` | One attempt to check a connection out of a pgcommon pool (WithConn, RunInTx and helpers), by outcome; error includes acquire timeouts (context deadline exceeded while waiting) and a closed pool. An attempt abandoned by the caller (context cancelled) is not counted under either outcome; its wait is still recorded in platform_db_pool_acquire_duration_seconds. |
| `platform_db_pool_acquire_duration_seconds` | platform-pgcommon | histogram (db_pool_acquire) | proposed | `pool` | Time a caller waited to check a connection out of a pgcommon pool, recorded for every attempt including failures — a saturation signal. |
| `platform_db_slow_queries_total` | platform-pgcommon | counter | proposed | `pool` | A statement whose wall time exceeded the pool's configured slow-query threshold (Config.SlowQueryThreshold). Counted for every occurrence, independent of log rate limiting. Library-internal statements (RLS GUC set_config, BEGIN / COMMIT / ROLLBACK, transaction timeouts, savepoints) are excluded. |
| `platform_db_transaction_retries_total` | platform-pgcommon | counter | proposed | `pool`, `reason`<br>`reason` ∈ `deadlock`, `serialization` | A transaction attempt that failed with a retryable PostgreSQL error and was retried by RunInTxWithRetry*: deadlock (SQLSTATE 40P01) or serialization failure (40001). |
| `platform_db_transaction_retries_exhausted_total` | platform-pgcommon | counter | proposed | `pool`, `reason`<br>`reason` ∈ `deadlock`, `serialization` | A RunInTxWithRetry* call that used every attempt and still failed with a retryable error — the operation failed for the caller. |
| `platform_db_pool_connections` | platform-pgcommon | gauge | proposed | `pool`, `state`<br>`state` ∈ `idle`, `acquired`, `constructing` | Connections currently held by a pgcommon pool, by state: idle (available), acquired (checked out), constructing (being dialled). Sampled at scrape time from the pool's statistics. |
| `platform_db_pool_max_connections` | platform-pgcommon | gauge | proposed | `pool` | The configured connection limit of a pgcommon pool (Config.MaxConns). |
| `platform_db_pool_empty_acquires_total` | platform-pgcommon | counter | proposed | `pool` | Cumulative acquires that had to wait because every connection was checked out (pool exhausted). A rising rate means the pool is undersized for the service's concurrency. |

## Tier 2: IAM domain-shared metrics (emitted by this service)

Built from the registry with `gincommon.NewSharedCounterVec` (`internal/adapter/outbound/metrics/business.go`, `buildCollectors`), so the name, help, labels and buckets are the registry's.

| Metric | Type | Status | Labels | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `iam_rls_violations_total` | counter | proposed | `violation_type` | Row-level-security violations recorded in the service's rls_violation_log, by violation_type. Fed from a periodic scrape of the log table, not from the request path. |

Registered for the `iam` domain but not emitted by this service: `iam_auth_events_total`, `iam_tenant_resolution_total`, `iam_identity_sync_total`, `iam_realm_operations_total`, `iam_auth_session_revoke_failed_total`, `iam_lifecycle_event_skipped_total`, `iam_lifecycle_event_lag_seconds`.

## Tier 3: service-specific metrics (`iam_audit_log_*`)

| Metric | Type | Labels | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `iam_audit_log_archive_lag_seconds` | gauge | - | Seconds past archival eligibility of the oldest still-attached partition (0 when none; RB-2). |
| `iam_audit_log_archive_partitions_total` | counter | `result`, `tier` | Per-tier archival outcomes, by tier and result (verified\|failed). |
| `iam_audit_log_archive_stalled_partitions` | gauge | - | Eligible partitions still attached past OPS_ARCHIVE_STALL_GRACE (AL-INV-9 held). Critical when > 0. |
| `iam_audit_log_catalog_plans_poll_total` | counter | `result` | CAT-I2 plan-map poll outcomes, by result (success\|error\|timeout; AL-D15). |
| `iam_audit_log_catalog_plans_stale_seconds` | gauge | - | Seconds since the last successful CAT-I2 poll (since start before the first). Stale-if-error masks outages (RB-8). |
| `iam_audit_log_default_partition_rows` | gauge | - | Rows in audit_events_default. Critical at > 0 (RB-3). |
| `iam_audit_log_directwrite_requests_total` | counter | `result`, `source_service` | AL-5/AL-6 entry outcomes, by source_service and result (created\|duplicate\|rejected\|error). RB-6. |
| `iam_audit_log_duplicate_events_total` | counter | `consumer` | Dedup hits (redeliveries / idempotent replays), by consumer (AL-INV-4). |
| `iam_audit_log_events_ingested_total` | counter | `entry_type`, `ingest_mode`, `source_service` | Audit rows persisted, by source_service, ingest_mode and entry_type. |
| `iam_audit_log_export_jobs_total` | counter | `status` | Export job lifecycle, by status (pending\|ready\|failed\|expired). |
| `iam_audit_log_ingest_lag_seconds` | histogram | - | recorded_at − occurred_at of newly persisted rows (HLD §3.4 SLO p99 < 50 ms async). |
| `iam_audit_log_query_archived_reads_total` | counter | - | Reads served (partly) from the S3 archive. |
| `iam_audit_log_query_window_clamped_total` | counter | `plan_code` | Queries whose explicit range was cut to the plan window, by plan_code (product signal, AL-INV-8). |
| `iam_audit_log_redaction_blocked_archive_total` | counter | - | Archival refused because a pending redaction task touches the partition (AL-INV-12). Critical; near zero. |
| `iam_audit_log_redaction_pending_tasks` | gauge | - | Redaction tasks pending longer than OPS_REDACTION_PENDING_AGE. Critical at > 0 (RB-7). |
| `iam_audit_log_redaction_tasks_total` | counter | `status` | GDPR redaction task outcomes, by status (applied\|not_applicable\|missed\|pending=apply failed). missed = archived rows retained (AL-Q15), routine; pending needs action (RB-7). |
| `iam_audit_log_retention_pruned_total` | counter | `tier` | Partition drops reconciled, by tier (§8.6). |
| `iam_audit_log_unknown_event_total` | counter | `source_service` | Unrecognized event types persisted as <domain>.unknown, by source_service (AL-EVT-4). Warning: extend the taxonomy. |
